name: צוּרִישַׁדָּי
summary: A man of Simeon in the wilderness, known only as the father of Shelumiel, the prince of Simeon at the numbering, at the offering of the altar and in the march from Sinai (Num 1:6; 2:12; 7:36, 41; 10:19). It is צוּר “rock” with the ־ִי of “my”, and שַׁדַּי, the name God gave himself to the fathers (Gen 17:1; Exo 6:3): “my rock is Shaddai”, as David says “my God, my rock” (Psa 18:3), and as the Levite Zuriel’s name says “my rock is God” (Num 3:35). Twice the text writes it as two words, צוּרִי שַׁדָּי (Num 2:12; 10:19).

evidence.note: Over the host of the tribe of the sons of Simeon, Shelumiel son of צוּרִי שַׁדָּי.
Simeon camping beside Reuben, its prince Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai.
Shelumiel son of Zurishaddai brings Simeon’s offering on the fifth day (and 7:41).
אֵלִי צוּרִי, “my God, my rock”: the same צוּרִי, “my rock”, said of God.
“I am אֵל שַׁדַּי; walk before me and be perfect.”
He appeared to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob as אֵל שַׁדַּי.
צוּרִיאֵל, “my rock is God”, the same pattern with אֵל.

note: TIPNR keys Zurishaddai’s son Shelumiel to Benjamin; the text makes him prince of Simeon (Num 1:6; 2:12). In Num 2:12 and 10:19 the name is written צוּרִי־שַׁדָּי / צוּרִי שַׁדָּי, and the corpus tags the צוּרִי part with the verb and rock keys, so the name’s r.bn.ae key covers only the one-word spellings and the שַׁדָּי halves. The ־ִי may be “my” or a joining vowel (“rock of Shaddai”). The other Shaddai names of these lists are שְׁדֵיאוּר and עַמִּישַׁדָּי.
